opportunity_model.methodology_html: Volume = Google Ads monthly searches in the Miami metro (DataForSEO). Potential clicks = volume x target click-through if MIA reaches a realistic top-3 local + organic position (35% if ranked 1-3 today, 28% if 4-10, 18% if 11-30, 15% if not yet ranking). Potential leads = potential clicks x 2.0% lead rate — conservative: MIA's blog-diluted site-wide rate is 0.8% (GA4), commercial-rental pages typically run 3-5%. Leads count form_submit + contact_form_submit only; phone, email and GBP→site clicks are tracked separately.

serp_audit.intro: We ran a live SERP capture (Miami, desktop + mobile) on the strongest zero-click query to find where the clicks are going.

queries.client_title: Premier Photo Booth Rental Miami | MIA Photo Booth
queries.diagnosis: Position 4.1 is the organic rank — but the visible top of the page is a 3-business local pack (Captured Fun, Luxe Booth, South Florida Photo Booth Vibes), and MIA is not in it. Below the pack sit three organic competitors, so MIA's listing is the 7th block on desktop and the 13th block on mobile. The local pack absorbs the local-intent clicks (the exact clicks the GBP-category fix targets), and the page that ranks is the generic homepage whose title says nothing about "Social" — so even the organic listing under-matches the query. No AI Overview, no ads — this is pure local-pack + organic-competition burial.
queries.fix: Two levers: (1) the GBP-category fix earns a place in the local pack that's currently taking the clicks; (2) a dedicated Social Booth page (title + H1 with "Social Photo Booth Rental Miami") converts the 13K impressions the homepage currently wastes.

queries.diagnosis: MIA ranks a blog post (/post/glam-photo-booths-for-brides) at organic #10 on desktop, and it falls out of the top 30 on mobile entirely. A commercial "glam booth" query is being answered with informational content that can't rank or convert — the blog-vs-commercial gap, made concrete.
queries.fix: Build/upgrade a commercial Glam Booth service page and wire the blog post to it; the blog earns the impressions, the service page should earn the click.

sept_dip.headline: A one-month Maps reach collapse in Sept 2025 — diagnosed, and already recovered.
sept_dip.what: Across all 8 tracked queries, MIA's grid presence collapsed in the early-Sept scans (top-3 cells 67 → 2; reach roughly halved) then fully recovered by the early-Oct scans (top-3 back to 74, reach above August).

ruled_out.label: Not a scan/data artifact
ruled_out.detail: Every Sept scan still captured the full 169-cell grid with ~3,380 rows and more competing businesses than August — the scan saw everything; only MIA shrank.

ruled_out.label: Not a delisting or suspension
ruled_out.detail: The Place ID was unchanged throughout (…RC9z24TEIGxg) and the review count kept climbing through the dip (92 → 94 → 97) — the profile stayed live and active the whole time.

ruled_out.label: Not a website problem
ruled_out.detail: GSC organic impressions were normal in September, and GA4 shows website sessions actually rose in Sept (212 → 447) with leads up (9 → 11). The website was growing while only the Maps pack compressed.

sept_dip.cause: The dip coincides with core-profile edits in the same window: a business-name change (MIA Photo Booth → "MIA Photo Booth - No.1 Photo Booth Rental", first visible in the Oct scans) and primary-category churn (Photography service ↔ Party equipment rental service). Editing core GBP fields routinely triggers a Google re-review that temporarily compresses a profile's grid reach — which matches the shape exactly: one month down, full recovery the next.
sept_dip.takeaway: Two things follow. (1) The profile is resilient and responsive — it bounced back above its prior reach within one cycle, which means a correct category fix should propagate fast. (2) GBP edits must be made deliberately, one at a time, with a 2-4 week settling window expected — so the Month-1 category change is sequenced first and alone, and we hold other core-field edits until it settles.

market.summary_html: The Maps leaderboard is reshuffling. Across the tracking window the prior leaders slid — Glam Shots down 283 top-3 cells, VIP Party Photo Booth down 381 — while three brands rose from near-zero: Captured Fun (+358), Luxe Booth (+319), Capture Pod (+274). That's category-flux — brands that align their GBP correctly climb fast. MIA's own movement and how it stacks against the field is below: the foundation is there, the top-3 conversion is what the 90-day plan unlocks.

tldr: The Maps gap is structural, not effort. MIA's Google Business profile primary category is Photography service; five of the eight top-3 dominators citywide run Photo booth as primary (Glam Shots wins 419 top-3 cells with only 15 reviews — the category match is doing the lifting). On top of that, the site footer phone is (786) 973-9973 — the GBP's chat/SMS number — while the GBP primary phone is (786) 833-7645; that NAP mismatch suppresses the site→GBP trust signal. Fix those two and the foundation (124 backlinks · 103 reviews · 739-cell average reach · organic clicks 26 → 768 in 5 months = a 30× HQDM-tenure climb) is positioned to convert.

headline.h2: Root cause is two GBP-level fixes — not site depth
headline.lede: Across 11 months of LD scans (Aug 5 2025 → May 6 2026), MIA's average rank sits at 10.69 on the latest scan (weighted across 8 tracked queries) with 43 top-3 cells out of 663 cells reached. Organic clicks have grown 30× — from 26/mo at engagement start to a peak of 768 in Jan '26. The two highest-intent Maps terms ("wedding photo booth rental" and "360 photo booth rental") show zero top-3 cells in the latest scan, and the tracked queries are still mostly outside the local pack — the gap is where the GBP-category fix targets.

connection.intro: Five elements of the website↔GBP handshake. The site is built — 27 area pages, 6 service pages, 60 blog posts — but the bones aren't connected. The most consequential break is the phone number; the rest compound it.
connection.verdict: The website doesn't currently reinforce the GBP. Until the phone number, schema and URL structure match, every link Google follows from the GBP into the site reads as a weak association.

rows.detail: The GBP primary phone is (786) 833-7645. The site footer and every service/area page show (786) 973-9973 — which is the GBP's chat/SMS number.
rows.fix: Global replace across the theme. Keep the SMS number only on a dedicated "Text us" button (sms: protocol).

rows.detail: The homepage and area pages return no JSON-LD LocalBusiness or Service schema. The richest site→GBP signal is missing entirely.
rows.fix: Add LocalBusiness schema sitewide with sameAs to the GBP Maps CID + the 6 social profiles. Service schema per booth-type page. FAQPage on /frequently-asked-questions.

rows.fix: Add 3-paragraph "Booth types we bring to [city]" block on every area page + in-body CTAs on top blog posts pointing to booth-type service pages.
